🤖 Telling an AI coding agent to "be accessible" made its output slightly worse.

Not a hot take — a measured result: a 17.32% violation rate with accessibility-oriented prompts, 15.93% without (W4A'25). 84% of AI-generated pages carry accessibility issues anyway (W4A'24).

Instructions are not the fix. A loop is. So I built one 👇

1️⃣ Decide it in the plan, not the pull request
Drag-only reordering. Hover-only menus. Data that only exists as canvas pixels. Each is one sentence to change while scoping — a rewrite afterwards.

2️⃣ Make accessible markup the default output
Semantic HTML first, ARIA discipline, real keyboard contracts, visible focus, contrast that holds in light AND dark.

3️⃣ Verify in a browser, not in the model's imagination
Five passes — default, dark, forced-colors, reduced-motion, 320px reflow — plus the states it just built: dialog open, form in error. Failures go back, get fixed, re-audit until it converges. A demo page seeded with 163 failures → 0, no regressions.

4️⃣ Say what you could NOT check
The part I care about most. It never claims compliance. Of the 55 WCAG 2.2 A/AA criteria, only 17 have any automated rule — so every run prints what still needs a human, a screen reader, and disabled testers.

🐎 Old: audit the UI after it is built, when nobody wants to touch it.
🚗 New: the agent cannot call it done until it has checked its own work.

The challenge came from My Life My Voice and their AI For People kaupapa, at the Aotearoa AI Hackathon 2026 where I mentored at Auckland University of Technology. It is over, nobody is scoring this, and I sent it to them anyway.

MIT. npm i -g a11y-loop

Disabled testers, accessibility practitioners: tell me what it gets wrong 👇

Sid is 14 in the summer of 2006.

So was I — 10,000 km away, in China. 🎬

Last night at The Civic, opening night of Whānau Mārama New Zealand Film Festival Trust: New Zealand International Film Festival, I watched Big Girls Don't Cry: a girlhood I never lived, and recognised in almost every frame.

🎞️ @Paloma Schneideman's debut feature refuses to tidy up the parts of being 14 that most films smooth over — class shame, the hierarchy of older girls, the gap between who you are at home and who you are at the beach.

🗣️ But the moment I can't stop thinking about is this: Sid asks her Māori mother to speak English, because otherwise she can't follow her.

I know that scene from the inside.

I'm from Guangxi, a Zhuang autonomous region in southern China. My grandmother speaks Zhuang. My mother understands it but can't speak it. I have neither — Zhuang ended with me.

Cantonese is my mother tongue, and my mother's, and hers. I was schooled in Mandarin. The kids ten years younger than me don't use Cantonese at all.

Three generations. Two languages. Nobody decided it; it just went quiet.

So te reo isn't heritage decoration to me. It's a line of transmission, and it breaks softly enough that you can miss it happening in your own family.

🌱 And Sid keeps going. A queer coming-of-age story told without flinching: her body, her desire, her place among people who haven't decided whether to let her in. She gets it wrong, gets hurt, tries again. The bravery isn't in the big moments. It's in the trying.

I cried at the last scene between her and her father.

Thank you Vicky Pope for the invitation, and Dr Mahsa McCauley (Mohaghegh) , Gurleen Kaur and She Sharp for sending me — I was there for the community that has spent a decade bridging the gender gap in STEM in Aotearoa. Congratulations to @Paloma Schneideman and the team on bringing this one home from Sundance.

Were you at The Civic on Wednesday? Which scene stayed with you? 👇

🧭 An endpoint I'd monitored daily for three months started returning 404. I nearly published the wrong obituary. 🪦

Five days after I published a thread showing Suno's public /api/trending had been serving the same September-2024 snapshot for ~22 months, it went dark.

Obvious read: they deleted it. I had the write-up drafted and queued.

It was wrong. The disproving test was one request away, and I hadn't run it.

Here's what three passes over the same 404 actually taught me 👇

🔍 1/ A 404 answers "is this route here" — not "is this thing gone"
/api/trending was never the resource. It was an alias for one abandoned playlist object. The alias was removed; the object is still public at its own address and still returns 200.
→ Route ≠ resource. I collapsed the two and drew a conclusion from the wrong noun.

📈 2/ Frozen ≠ static
Membership hasn't meaningfully changed since Sept 2024 and can only shrink, by owner deletion. But the counters underneath never stopped: 5 of the 41 clips I track gained plays in four days.
→ It's a frozen 2024 playlist row joined against live clip rows.

🔓 3/ The removed route WAS the leak
Same object, two paths, two serializers. Through the old alias: 90 real remix-lineage pointers. Through the playlist path today: 0 real, 88 redacted to a zero UUID.
→ My lineage archive is sealed — not because data vanished, but because the path that skipped redaction did.

🚨 4/ Monitors decay silently
My schema-drift canary reported "ok" for weeks while watching an endpoint that no longer existed. It swallowed unreachable errors by design — a reasonable choice, until the world moved under it.
→ A monitor that cannot fail is not a monitor.

The mental shift:
🪦 Wrong → "it's deleted, the archive is sealed"
🔍 Right → "the door was removed, the room is still lit — and the door was the leak"

Both versions land on "sealed." Only one is reproducible. A conclusion that is right for the wrong reason still misleads whoever builds on it next. ✨

When did a monitor of yours last go green while measuring nothing? 👇

posts.text:
🔍 Suno's public "trending" API has been serving the same 49 songs since September 2024. Nobody noticed for 22 months.

I found it by accident, building something unrelated.

The lesson isn't about Suno. It's about what happens to systems nobody is watching.

Here's the forensics 👇

📅 1/ The data dated itself
All 49 clips were created inside one 72-hour window: Sept 15-17, 2024. A live chart on a platform generating millions of songs a month does not, by chance, contain only one weekend.

📸 2/ 84 daily captures, 0% turnover
I'd been snapshotting the endpoint every day since April — not for a thesis, just because instrumenting things is cheap. Same songs, same order, every day. The #1 clip gained 56 plays in three months.

🧊 3/ It's not a cache — it's the database
Two fetches 108 seconds apart: byte-identical. Then the header: Cf-Cache-Status: DYNAMIC.
→ Origin-served, not an edge cache
→ No stale cache to bust, because nothing is stale
→ The origin is faithfully serving a record nobody has written to since 2024

🚪 4/ The live product doesn't know it exists
Suno rebuilt Explore in May 2026 on curated shelves. I compared membership: zero overlap. Not one song in common.
→ Not a stale view of the live thing — an abandoned object that never got a deprecation

✍️ 5/ I had it wrong first
I'd already published a reading of this — "deliberately frozen, an editorial choice" — and built an instrument to measure the cadence of a feed I had already misclassified. The correction is in the write-up. You can't ask people to check your work while quietly deleting the version you got wrong.

The mental shift:
🗑️ Old frame → a 200 OK means the data is current
🔎 New frame → an endpoint answering politely tells you nothing about whether anyone still owns it

Fast-moving companies leave objects behind. No error, no 410 Gone — just a cheerful 200 and a payload from the deep past.

Instrument the boring things. The finding was free. I just had to be looking. ✨

Full method, evidence, and the correction: https://lnkd.in/dNZPjxJ8

🗂️ 1/ One source of truth — a single YAML "career database"
One file holds everything: identity, every project, every role, teaching, metrics.
→ Schema-validated on every build (JSON Resume + extensions) — invalid data ships nothing
→ 72 projects, 12 companies, 4 teaching cohorts — all traceable to one file
→ You curate the facts once, in one place. No copy-paste across five surfaces.

⚙️ 2/ One command renders every surface
A single build (and a GitHub Action on every push) regenerates:
→ the GitHub README
→ a Typst-compiled CV PDF
→ the LinkedIn payload — JSON + 17 markdown sections
→ the design tokens that keep it all visually consistent
The README is just one of the outputs, not the thing you edit.

🔄 3/ Live data, not stale screenshots
A refresh step pulls stars, forks, and commit dates straight from the GitHub API.
→ GitHub and LinkedIn stop drifting apart — same source, rendered twice
→ Your metrics update themselves; you stop maintaining numbers by hand.

🤖 4/ Make it machine-readable for the AI that now screens you
The same data emits llms.txt + schema.org JSON-LD.
→ Recruiter LLMs and AI search read your career as structured data, not scraped text
→ You control the canonical record the machines quote back

The mental shift:
📄 Old → a README you hand-type and watch drift out of date
🗂️ New → a README that's the rendered view of one validated career database

Your profile is a product. Give it a single source of truth and a build step. ✨

Extending Claude Code? 🛠️ Choosing the right way to integrate external tools can make or break your token spend and agent performance.

🔹 MCP Servers (The Heavy Lifters)
Think of this as dumping a massive, raw API directly into your environment. You get maximum flexibility, but it comes at a steep price—often preloading 50K+ tokens before you even type a prompt. Plus, the model has to figure out how to use those endpoints from scratch every single time.

🔹 Skills (The Game Changers)
These are simply SKILL.md files that encode your opinionated workflows. Instead of raw access, you bake in your preferences, defaults, and error handling. The secret weapon here is progressive disclosure—they only load into the context window when activated, saving massive amounts of tokens. They are also highly portable; write a Skill once, and it works across other filesystem-aware agents!

🔹 Slash Commands (The Daily Drivers)
Your built-in, frictionless shortcuts (like /simplify or /debug). Perfect for when you know exactly what needs executing and don't need the AI to spend time inferring your intent.

When building out AI agents, providing a structured, repeatable path (Skills) often outperforms throwing a raw API at the model (MCP). It leads to much more consistent, predictable outputs. 👌

What is AG-UI (Agent-User Interaction Protocol)?
It's an open, lightweight, event-based protocol designed to be the universal standard for connecting AI agents to front-end applications. Think of it as the missing link that enables fluent, real-time communication between your agent's backend and the user's screen.

🔹 AG-UI brings the agent's power directly to the user.

💬 Real-time agentic chat with streaming

Hot take: The AI race isn't about reaching infinite intelligence. It's about stopping at "good enough." 🤔

We're obsessed with AI benchmarks, but we're forgetting a key lesson from tech history: Diminishing Marginal Utility.

Remember when you upgraded your PC for a faster CPU? Now you upgrade your phone because the battery died. The core tech became "good enough."

AI is on the same trajectory. For most businesses, is an AI that's 99.5% accurate truly better than one that's 99% accurate if it costs 10x more? Probably not. The extra benefit (the marginal utility) just isn't there.

Once we hit "peak utility," the market will pivot. The winners won't be the ones with the highest IQ points for their models, but those who master the new game:

✅ Price: Making powerful AI accessible to everyone. 
✅ Usability: Creating products that are a joy to use. 
✅ Integration: Building tools that fit like a puzzle piece into your business.

The future isn't just a smarter brain 🧠, it's a practical, affordable, and indispensable tool. The real opportunity isn't just building the model, it's building the solution around it.

Agree or disagree? Let's discuss!

📚 Fascinating Research: Cache-Augmented Generation (CAG) vs RAG 🧠

Just came across this interesting research on LLM knowledge integration that I wanted to share! 📊

While Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has been widely adopted for knowledge tasks, researchers have proposed Cache-Augmented Generation (CAG) as an alternative approach.

✅ What caught my attention about CAG:
- Preloads knowledge into extended context windows instead of real-time retrieval
- Uses precomputed KV cache for faster inference
- Eliminates retrieval latency entirely

The potential benefits highlighted in the paper: 
- ⏱️ Reduced response times without retrieval overhead
- 🔄 More coherent responses through unified context
- ⚙️ Simpler system architecture with fewer components

Most suitable for scenarios with manageable knowledge bases like documentation, FAQs, or support resources.

The researchers' benchmarks on SQuAD and HotpotQA datasets showed promising results!

- Implementing absolute path references for Node.js executables and server scripts

The process required precise system path configurations, global npm package management, and detailed understanding of MCP server architecture. I successfully configured multiple servers including filesystem, GitHub, PostgreSQL, Puppeteer, and Brave Search integration.

All MCP servers now connect and function flawlessly, enabling seamless interaction between Claude and various external services. The solution has been documented and shared with the MCP community on GitHub to help others facing similar challenges.

🧠 Diving into SOLID principles: Single Responsibility Principle (SRP) 🏗️

SRP states that a class should have only one reason to change. In other words, it should have a single, well-defined responsibility. Here's why it's crucial:

✅ Enhances maintainability
✅ Improves code readability
✅ Reduces the risk of bugs when modifying code

Consider a User class in a web application. Instead of burdening it with multiple responsibilities like data storage, validation, and authentication, we can split these into separate classes:

🔹 User: Manages user details
🔹 UserValidator: Handles data validation
🔹 Authenticator: Manages authentication

This separation allows for easier maintenance and extension as our project grows. It's not just about writing code—it's about designing systems that can evolve gracefully over time. 🌱

#SoftwareDevelopment #SOLID #SingleResponsibilityPrinciple #CleanCode #BestPractices
